issue: Is attempted Hobbs Act robbery categorically a 'crime of violence' under the elements clause of 18 U.S.C. § 924(c)(3)(A)?

sides.position: Attempted Hobbs Act robbery is categorically a crime of violence under the elements clause, because an attempt to commit a crime of violence (with intent and a substantial step) qualifies as an attempted use or threatened use of force.
cases: United States v. Smith, 957 F.3d 590 (5th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Ingram, 947 F.3d 1021 (7th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Dominguez, 954 F.3d 1251 (9th Cir. 2020)
United States v. St. Hubert, 909 F.3d 335 (11th Cir. 2018)
United States v. Walker, 990 F.3d 316 (3d Cir. 2021)

sides.position: Attempted Hobbs Act robbery is not categorically a crime of violence, because a nonviolent substantial step toward threatening force does not involve the use, attempted use, or threatened use of physical force under the plain text of § 924(c)(3)(A).
cases: United States v. Taylor, 979 F.3d 203 (4th Cir. 2020)

quote: Our sister courts of appeals are split on the answer to that question.
cite: United States v. Marcus Walker, 990 F.3d 316 (3rd Cir. 2021)
